\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{باغ} (bāgh)}{باغ (bāgh)}]{\ur{باغ} (bāgh) — a garden}

\label{lesson:UR-C512-bagh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to blow (on), then the Urdu for to give (someone) a taste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{باغ}}
\textbf{\ur{باغ}} — \emph{bāgh} — \textquotedblleft{}a garden\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمارے} \ur{گھر} \ur{کے} \ur{پیچھے} \ur{ایک} \ur{باغ} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamāre ghar ke pīchhe ek bāgh hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a garden behind our house.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{باغ}} (\emph{bāgh}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{bāgh}, \textquotedblleft{}a garden, an orchard\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāgh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bāgh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamāre ghar ke pīchhe ek bāgh hai.} — There is a garden behind our house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to blow (on), then the Urdu for to give (someone) a taste, then say \emph{bāgh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{باغ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A garden\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کیاری} (kyārī)}{کیاری (kyārī)}]{\ur{کیاری} (kyārī) — a flower bed}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to give (someone) a taste, then the Urdu for a garden.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سینچنا} (sīṅchnā)}{سینچنا (sīṅchnā)}]{\ur{سینچنا} (sīṅchnā) — to water (plants); to irrigate}

\label{lesson:UR-C512-sinchna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a flower bed, then the Urdu for fertiliser.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سینچنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سینچنا}} — \emph{sīṅchnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to water (plants); to irrigate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مالی} \ur{ہر} \ur{شام} \ur{باغ} \ur{سینچتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mālī har shām bāgh sīṅchtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gardener waters the garden every evening.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کیاری} \ur{سینچی}, \emph{us ne kyārī sīṅchī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سینچنا}} (\emph{sīṅchnā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{siñcati}, \textquotedblleft{}pours out, sprinkles\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13394).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اکھاڑنا} (ukhāṛnā)}{اکھاڑنا (ukhāṛnā)}]{\ur{اکھاڑنا} (ukhāṛnā) — to pull up; to uproot}

\label{lesson:UR-C512-ukharna-uproot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for fertiliser, then the Urdu for to water (plants).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اکھاڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اکھاڑنا}} — \emph{ukhāṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pull up; to uproot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مالی} \ur{نے} \ur{کیاری} \ur{سے} \ur{گھاس} \ur{اکھاڑی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mālī ne kyārī se ghās ukhāṛī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gardener pulled the grass out of the flower bed.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پودا} \ur{اکھاڑا}, \emph{us ne paudā ukhāṛā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اکھاڑنا}} (\emph{ukhāṛnā}) is inherited from \emph{*utskarati}, \textquotedblleft{}digs out\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs, under which it lists the Hindi verb meaning \textquotedblleft{}to uproot\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1895).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ukhāṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mālī ne kyārī se ghās ukhāṛī.} — The gardener pulled the grass out of the flower bed.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for fertiliser, then the Urdu for to water (plants), then say \emph{ukhāṛnā} again
\end{itemize}
